title: What do masterchain and shard blocks mean?
description:
The masterchain holds global configuration and references shardchain states. Most user accounts live in the basechain, which can be divided into shards. A block is identified by its workchain, shard and sequence number together; a sequence number alone is not a network-wide block height.

The top strip shows basechain blocks. Open the search menu and choose Masterchain under SELECTED to view masterchain blocks. Choose a shard when several are active. Open a block to inspect its transactions; masterchain blocks also link their referenced shards.

title: How are transactions, messages and traces related?
description:
A transaction records one account processing a message or a system operation. Messages connect accounts; processing an incoming message may create outgoing messages and further transactions. A trace follows those linked transactions.

Use the transaction page for local execution, messages for transfers between contracts, and the trace for the wider operation. TON fundamentals.

title: What is logical time?
description: Logical time (LT) orders transactions and messages. It is separate from the Unix timestamp shown as the transaction date. Account history uses LT as its pagination cursor; preserve it as an exact integer string.

title: Where did the fee go?
description:
Execution can include storage, credit, compute, action and bounce phases. The transaction page shows total fees and the recorded phase details, including gas use, forwarding costs and exit codes. A failed operation can still pay fees.

GRAM is TON’s native currency and uses 9 decimal places: 1 GRAM = 1,000,000,000 nanograms. A message value and the transaction fee describe different amounts.

title: What does bounced or failed mean?
description:
A bounced message returns a response when a bounceable message cannot be processed under the applicable rules. It is a separate message with its own value and costs. Check the transaction result, compute and action results, and outgoing messages together.

A confirmed transaction can have failed execution. One successful transaction also does not establish that every later transaction in its trace succeeded. TON blockchain specification.

title: Is confirmation the same as a complete operation?
description: Confirmation means the transaction is included in its block. A multi-contract operation can involve additional transactions and messages. Inspect the full trace and final recipient rather than treating the first transaction as the whole transfer.

title: What does an account page show?
description:
Accounts show their GRAM balance, state, last activity and detected contract interfaces. History groups recognized actions; Transactions lists account transactions. Jettons and NFTs have separate tabs.

The Contract tab contains state, code and data, read-only methods, and available staking, multisig, subscription and DeFi records. Expand Account details for additional fields and extra currencies.

title: Why can the same account have different addresses?
description:
TON accounts can be written as a raw workchain and hexadecimal account ID or a user-friendly address. Bounceability and network flags can change the user-friendly representation without changing the underlying account.

Search accepts TON addresses and .ton names. DNS resolution links to the resolved account; a domain name is not a substitute for checking the account address.

title: Can I read a smart contract?
description:
Select a listed getter in the Contract tab and supply its arguments when needed. Reads return a result without signing a transaction. Arguments may be comma-separated strings or a JSON array of strings; preserve large integers as strings.

Account details preserve code, data and storage fields. Inspection shows recognized interfaces and available compiler information.

title: What does the validators page show?
description: The validators page shows the election timestamps, total and minimum stake, and participating validator accounts, stakes and ADNL addresses. These fields describe the displayed election data; an address holding stake is not automatically the producer of a particular block.

title: How do jettons work?
description:
A jetton has a master contract and individual jetton-wallet contracts for holders. Identify it by the master address, not its name or symbol. The jetton page shows supply, decimals, administration and holders.

Display balances using the jetton’s own decimals. Do not assume every jetton has 9 decimals. Jetton standard.

title: Why can a jetton’s displayed balance differ from its on-chain amount?
description:
Some jettons use a display multiplier. Current wallet balances, holder balances and total supply apply that ratio with exact rounding, then the token’s decimals. Expand Amount details to see the on-chain amount, raw units and ratio.

Historical transfers retain their recorded on-chain quantity; a current multiplier is not evidence of the multiplier at that time. Scaled UI jetton standard.

title: What identifies an NFT?
description:
The NFT item’s contract address is its identity. Its collection, owner and item index are separate fields. Collection membership verification checks the item’s relationship to a collection; it does not establish that its image, name or seller is trustworthy.

Item details show the exact index when confirmed by the NFT contract. A display number in an NFT’s name need not equal its on-chain index.

title: Where do images and attributes come from?
description:
TEP-64 supports on-chain, off-chain and combined metadata. The NFT page displays names, descriptions, images and attributes, with the full metadata available to expand. Media or metadata hosted elsewhere can change or become unavailable.

Open animations explicitly from the item page. Missing media does not erase the NFT’s contract or ownership record. Token metadata standard.

title: Why is an NFT owned by a sale contract?
description:
A listed NFT may be held by a marketplace sale contract. Wallet NFT lists include recognized indirect sale ownership. The item page separates the on-chain owner, seller, sale contract and price currency.

A sale listing is not a completed transfer. Use transfer history to follow changes, and the collection page to browse its items.

title: Are all Telegram gifts visible on-chain?
description:
No. A gift must exist as a TON NFT to have an on-chain item address and ownership record here. Telegram gifts, collectible usernames and numbers can have associated TON NFTs, but a Telegram profile or ordinary username alone does not prove wallet ownership.

A collectible may be displayed on a Telegram profile while its owner remains a TON wallet. Check its item address, collection and current owner. Telegram collectible gifts.

title: How do I see all the NFTs in an account or collection?
description: Use Load more below the NFT list to continue through the collection or wallet. The NFTs tab includes each returned item separately, with its full name and link to item details. A wallet’s NFT collection and its transaction history are independent lists.

title: What do recognition labels mean?
description: Collection membership, trust classification and marketplace approvals are distinct facts. Recognized names and images are not ownership proofs. Compare contract addresses and collection links before treating two similarly named assets as the same token.

title: How does automatic routing work?
description: Paste an address, transaction hash, message hash, block number or .ton name into search. Automatic Routing lets the taxi find its chain. Choosing a native explorer keeps that chain’s search available; View Hub returns to tx.taxi.

title: What does Updates delayed mean?
description: The last available data remains visible while fresh updates are delayed. Retry an unavailable section to load it again. An empty list and an unavailable list are different states.

title: Can tx.taxi reverse a transaction?
description: tx.taxi displays public chain data. It cannot sign transactions, access private keys or reverse a transfer. For wallet or exchange account support, contact the service that submitted the operation.

title: Values and pagination
description:
All routes below use GET. Precision-sensitive integers are decimal strings; parse them with arbitrary-precision arithmetic. GRAM balances and fees are nanograms. Jetton amounts use their declared decimals.

Paginated responses include _paging. Continue only while hasMore is true, using nextOffset, nextBeforeLt or nextBefore for the matching endpoint. List limits are capped at 100; block lists at 16.

_meta.observedAt identifies the observation time and _meta.stale marks retained data. HTTP 400 means invalid input, 404 means not found, and 503 means temporarily unavailable.

title: Network overview
description: Returns the selected workchain and shard, recent blocks, observed history, observation time and stale state. The default is the basechain. Use workchain=-1 for the masterchain, or workchain=0&shard=... for an active basechain shard. activeShards lists available shards; masterchainHead is the network masterchain head.

title: Blocks
description: Returns blocks from one workchain and shard in descending sequence order. The default is the basechain; use workchain=-1 for masterchain blocks. Continue with before=_paging.nextBefore and retain workchain and shard from the response; the boundary is exclusive. Pagination stops at a shard split or merge.

title: Block details
description: Use a sequence number or the full (workchain,shard,seqno) identifier. A sequence number uses the selected workchain and shard; without a selection, it uses the host’s default workchain and root shard. Returns hashes, timestamps, logical times, references and value-flow fields.

title: Block transactions
description: Returns the transactions included in the specified block.

title: Masterchain shard references
description: Use a masterchain sequence number or masterchain block identifier. Returns the corresponding shard references.

title: Network transactions
description: Returns transactions across the shards in one masterchain interval. Continue within that interval using master_seqno=_paging.masterSeqno and offset=_paging.nextOffset. When nextOffset is null, continue with before=_paging.nextBefore instead. Limits are capped at 50.

title: Masterchain transactions
description: Returns transactions from one masterchain block. Continue with before=_paging.nextBefore. These are masterchain transactions, not all transactions across every shard.

title: Validators
description: Returns validator election information, stake amounts and validator entries.

title: Domain details
description: Domain identity, expiry and linked NFT. Append /resolve for wallet, site, storage and resolver records, or /bids for bid history.

title: DNS auctions
description: Current domain auctions. Select ton or t.me.

title: Expiring domains
description: Returns domains approaching expiry. The optional period is the number of days before expiry.

title: Staking pool
description: Pool stake, nominators, cycle, implementation and annual percentage yield. Append /history for observed APY history.

title: Extra currency
description: Currency ID, symbol, decimals and image.

title: Extra currency history
description: Account events for the selected currency. Continue with before_lt.

title: Block BOC
description: Downloads the block as a binary Bag of Cells.

title: Raw configuration
description: Raw network configuration. Add master_seqno to request a historical masterchain configuration.

title: Blockchain configuration
description: Returns decoded blockchain configuration parameters. Add master_seqno for a historical masterchain configuration.

title: GRAM exchange rates
description: Returns GRAM rates in AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, JPY and USD.

title: Transaction details
description: Returns the account transaction, messages, fees, phases and state changes, plus available trace and interpreted event details. relatedUnavailable identifies related sections that could not be loaded.

title: Transaction by message hash
description: Finds the transaction associated with the supplied message hash.

title: Trace
description: Returns the linked transaction tree with child traces and execution details.

title: Resolve search input
description: Resolves a TON account, NFT, collection, jetton, transaction, message hash, block identifier or .ton domain. Returns the entity type and identifier.

title: Account details
description: Returns balance, status, contract interfaces, available blockchain state and DNS names. State can include code, data, storage information and extra currencies.

title: Account transactions
description: Lists account transactions. Continue with before_lt=_paging.nextBeforeLt; after_lt is also accepted.

title: Account transfers and events
description: Returns interpreted actions and their statuses. Continue with before_lt.

title: Jetton balances
description: Returns balances with master-contract metadata and the account’s jetton-wallet addresses.

title: Account NFTs
description: Returns NFT items, including recognized indirect sale ownership by default. Filter with collection, or use indirect_ownership=false for direct ownership only. Continue with offset=_paging.nextOffset.

title: NFT operations
description: Returns the account’s NFT operations. Continue with before_lt.

title: Jetton history
description: Returns jetton events for the account. Continue with before_lt.

title: Contract inspection
description: Returns available contract inspection details and recognized interfaces.

title: Read a contract method
description: Executes a read-only getter. Supply each argument as a repeated args parameter, for example ?args=123&args=456. Arguments remain strings and may contain integer, address or BOC values accepted by the method.

title: Staking pools
description: Returns the account’s nominator-pool positions.

title: Multisig contract
description: Returns the multisig contract’s threshold, signers, proposers, sequence number and orders. Use the plural route below to find multisigs associated with a signer’s wallet.

title: Multisig records
description: Returns multisig records associated with the account.

title: Subscriptions
description: Returns the account’s subscription records.

title: DeFi assets
description: Returns recognized DeFi positions and assets for the account.

title: NFT item
description: Returns the item’s owner, collection, metadata, media previews, trust and sale fields. indexVerified indicates whether index was confirmed by get_nft_data; the original index remains in indexed_index.

title: Soulbound NFT details
description: For a soulbound NFT, returns the authority address and revocation timestamp from its contract. A zero revocation timestamp means not revoked. Soulbound items are non-transferable.

title: NFT history
description: Returns events for an individual NFT. Continue with before_lt.

title: Collection details
description: Returns the collection’s owner, content, metadata and previews. When indexVerified is true, next_item_index is confirmed by the collection getter; it is not necessarily a total item count.

title: Collection items
description: Returns NFT items from a collection. Continue with offset=_paging.nextOffset.

title: Jetton details
description: Returns master-contract metadata, total supply, administration, decimals and holder count.

title: Jetton holders
description: Returns holder entries under addresses. Continue with offset=_paging.nextOffset. Balance values use the jetton’s decimals.

title: Connect
description: Connect to the same host at /api/v1/ws and send init for the current snapshot. Basechain blocks are selected by default. Add ?workchain=-1 for the masterchain, or ?workchain=0&shard=... for a basechain shard. Use the REST API for individual accounts, NFTs, transactions and traces.

title: Current snapshot
description: The response includes recent normalized blocks from the selected workchain and shard, plus a ton object with the head, observed history, observation time and stale state. Use ton.head for complete selected-block fields and ton.masterchainHead for the network masterchain head. Send {"action":"select","workchain":-1} to switch an open connection to the masterchain.

title: Keep the connection active
description: Send a ping to check the connection. On reconnect, send init again to obtain the current snapshot.

title: Delayed updates
description: When ton.stale is true, retain the last available blocks and mark them as delayed. ton.observedAt is the observation timestamp. WebSocket connection health alone does not establish data freshness.
